### Chapter 17: Expressing Views {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: sol-17-setup
#| include: false
source("R/_common.R")
library(tidypm)
library(knitr)

R  <- as_xts_pm(sim_class_returns_monthly, date, class, return)
rf <- sim_riskfree_monthly$return
Re <- R - rf
stopifnot(ncol(Re) == 16L, !anyNA(Re))
N <- ncol(Re); T <- nrow(Re)
mu_s <- colMeans(Re); S <- stats::cov(Re)

# The prior, as in the chapter and in chapter 6.
eq_ids     <- sim_assets$asset_id[sim_assets$asset_class == "equity"]
region_of  <- setNames(sim_assets$region, sim_assets$asset_id)
eq_classes <- grep("_equity$", colnames(Re), value = TRUE)
cap_region <- sim_marketcap_weekly |>
  dplyr::filter(asset %in% eq_ids) |>
  dplyr::mutate(class = paste0(region_of[asset], "_equity")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(date, class) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cap = sum(market_cap), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = cap) |>
  dplyr::arrange(date)
cap_mat <- as.matrix(cap_region[, eq_classes])
d <- zoo::index(Re)
W_eq <- t(vapply(seq_along(d), function(i) {
  cutoff <- if (i == 1) d[1] - 31 else d[i - 1]
  j <- max(which(cap_region$date <= cutoff))
  cap_mat[j, ] / sum(cap_mat[j, ])
}, numeric(length(eq_classes))))
colnames(W_eq) <- eq_classes
block <- c(equity = 0.40, government = 0.40, credit = 0.15, commodity = 0.05)
W16 <- matrix(0, nrow(Re), N, dimnames = list(NULL, colnames(Re)))
for (r in sub("_equity$", "", eq_classes)) {
  s <- W_eq[, paste0(r, "_equity")]
  W16[, paste0(r, "_equity")]     <- block[["equity"]]     * s
  W16[, paste0(r, "_government")] <- block[["government"]] * s
  W16[, paste0(r, "_credit")]     <- block[["credit"]]     * s
}
W16[, "GLOBAL_commodity"] <- block[["commodity"]]
mkt16_e <- rowSums(W16 * zoo::coredata(Re))
delta16 <- mean(mkt16_e) / stats::var(mkt16_e)
w_mkt   <- colMeans(W16)
mu_eq   <- setNames(delta16 * as.numeric(S %*% w_mkt), colnames(Re))

tangency_lo <- function(mu, S) {
  if (max(mu) <= 0) return(setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(mu)), names(mu)))
  N <- length(mu)
  sol <- quadprog::solve.QP(Dmat = 2 * S, dvec = rep(0, N),
                            Amat = cbind(mu, diag(N)), bvec = c(1, rep(0, N)), meq = 1)
  w <- pmax(sol$solution, 0)
  setNames(w / sum(w), names(mu))
}
bl_post <- function(mu, S, P, q, conf, tau = 1, diagonal = FALSE) {
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(P), names(mu)), nrow(P) == length(q))
  Omega <- (1 - conf) / conf * P %*% (tau * S) %*% t(P)
  if (diagonal) Omega <- diag(diag(Omega), nrow = nrow(P))
  M <- solve(P %*% (tau * S) %*% t(P) + Omega)
  list(mu = setNames(mu + as.numeric((tau * S) %*% t(P) %*% M %*% (q - P %*% mu)), names(mu)),
       Omega = Omega)
}
eff_n <- function(p) exp(-sum(p[p > 0] * log(p[p > 0])))
p0 <- rep(1 / T, T); Aeq0 <- matrix(1, 1, T)

P <- matrix(0, 2, N, dimnames = list(c("credit_spread", "commodity"), colnames(Re)))
P["credit_spread", "US_credit"] <- 1; P["credit_spread", "EU_credit"] <- -1
P["commodity", "GLOBAL_commodity"] <- 1
q <- c(credit_spread = 0.02, commodity = 0.04) / 12
prior_views <- as.numeric(P %*% mu_eq)
```

#### Exercise 1

```{r}
#| label: sol-17-ex1
full <- bl_post(mu_eq, S, P, q, conf = 0.5)
diag <- bl_post(mu_eq, S, P, q, conf = 0.5, diagonal = TRUE)
pooled <- 0.5 * prior_views + 0.5 * unname(q)
rbind(full     = as.numeric(P %*% full$mu) * 12,
      diagonal = as.numeric(P %*% diag$mu) * 12,
      pooling  = pooled * 12) |> round(4)
c(off_diagonal_of_PSP = (P %*% S %*% t(P))[1, 2],
  view_correlation    = stats::cov2cor(P %*% S %*% t(P))[1, 2],
  max_mean_gap_pp     = max(abs(full$mu - diag$mu)) * 1200)
```

With the full matrix, @eq-17-pooling holds exactly for both views. With a
diagonal $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ it does not: the credit-spread view lands at
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * as.numeric(P %*% diag$mu)[1] * 12)` rather than
the midpoint `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * pooled[1] * 12)`, because the
bracketed matrix in @eq-17-posterior is no longer a scalar multiple of
$\boldsymbol{P}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\boldsymbol{P}'$. The off-diagonal element
is the covariance between the two view portfolios, here a correlation of
`r sprintf("%.2f", stats::cov2cor(P %*% S %*% t(P))[1, 2])`: under the full
convention an error in one view is assumed to co-move with an error in the
other as the portfolios do, under the diagonal convention the two errors are
independent. The conventions coincide only when the view portfolios are
uncorrelated, and the largest gap in a posterior mean here is
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(full$mu - diag$mu)) * 1200)` percentage points a
year.

#### Exercise 2

```{r}
#| label: sol-17-ex2
V <- as.numeric(zoo::coredata(Re[, "US_equity"])); m0 <- mean(V); s0 <- stats::sd(V)
vol_view <- function(r) {
  e <- suppressMessages(EntropyProg(p0, Aeq = rbind(Aeq0, V, V^2), beq = c(1, m0, (r * s0)^2 + m0^2)))
  p <- as.numeric(e$p_)
  mm <- meucci.moments(Re, p)
  w <- tangency_lo(setNames(as.numeric(mm$mu), colnames(Re)), mm$sigma)
  top <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]
  list(n_eff = eff_n(p), top = fmt_model(zoo::index(Re)[top]), top_date = zoo::index(Re)[top],
       top_abs_dev = abs(V[top] - m0) / s0, us_credit = w[["US_credit"]])
}
half <- vol_view(0.5); more <- vol_view(1.5)
in_shock <- sum(in_episode(more$top_date, "liquidity_shock"))
stopifnot(in_shock >= 1L, !any(in_episode(half$top_date, "liquidity_shock")))
tibble::tibble(view = c("50% of sample volatility", "150% of sample volatility"),
               n_eff = c(half$n_eff, more$n_eff),
               most_probable_months = c(paste(half$top, collapse = ", "), paste(more$top, collapse = ", ")),
               their_distance_in_sd = c(paste(sprintf("%.1f", half$top_abs_dev), collapse = ", "),
                                        paste(sprintf("%.1f", more$top_abs_dev), collapse = ", ")),
               us_credit_weight = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * c(half$us_credit, more$us_credit))) |>
  kable(align = "lrllr")
```

Halving the volatility keeps `r sprintf("%.0f", half$n_eff)` effective
months and loads the months closest to the mean; raising it by half keeps
`r sprintf("%.0f", more$n_eff)` and loads the months furthest from it,
`r in_shock` of the three most probable in the liquidity shock. `US_credit` goes to
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * half$us_credit)` of the tangency portfolio under
the first view and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * more$us_credit)` under the
second, because the series' left tail is in exactly the months the second
view weights up. A volatility view on one equity market is a view on the
crisis months, and every series with a tail in them is re-rated.

#### Exercise 3

```{r}
#| label: sol-17-ex3
P_a <- matrix(0, 1, N, dimnames = list("JP_vs_UScredit", colnames(Re)))
P_a[1, "JP_equity"] <- 1; P_a[1, "US_credit"] <- -1
spread_eq <- as.numeric(P_a %*% mu_eq); q_a <- spread_eq + 0.03 / 12; c_a <- 0.5
set.seed(1602)
i_top <- match("JP_equity", colnames(Re)); i_bot <- match("US_credit", colnames(Re))
cb    <- setNames(centroid.buckets(list(i_bot, setdiff(seq_len(N), c(i_bot, i_top)), i_top)), colnames(Re))
kappa <- c_a * (q_a - spread_eq) / (cb[["JP_equity"]] - cb[["US_credit"]])
mu_C  <- mu_eq + kappa * cb

# The same two numbers as absolute views through the posterior formula.
P_2 <- matrix(0, 2, N, dimnames = list(c("JP_equity", "US_credit"), colnames(Re)))
P_2["JP_equity", "JP_equity"] <- 1; P_2["US_credit", "US_credit"] <- 1
q_2 <- mu_C[c("JP_equity", "US_credit")]
mu_2 <- bl_post(mu_eq, S, P_2, q_2, c_a)$mu

W <- cbind(market = w_mkt, centroid_direct = tangency_lo(mu_C, S), centroid_as_views = tangency_lo(mu_2, S))
moved <- function(w) sum(abs(w - w_mkt) > 0.005)
others <- setdiff(colnames(Re), c("JP_equity", "US_credit"))
ratio  <- W[others, "centroid_as_views"] / w_mkt[others]
stopifnot(diff(range(ratio)) < 1e-6)      # every other weight is the market weight, rescaled by one factor
c(direct_moved = moved(W[, "centroid_direct"]), as_views_moved = moved(W[, "centroid_as_views"]),
  direct_turnover = sum(abs(W[, "centroid_direct"] - w_mkt)) / 2,
  as_views_turnover = sum(abs(W[, "centroid_as_views"] - w_mkt)) / 2)
round(W[abs(W[, "centroid_direct"] - w_mkt) > 0.005, ] * 100, 1)
```

Through @eq-17-posterior the two numbers reach the optimizer as
$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\boldsymbol{P}'$ times a coefficient, so `US_government`,
`EU_credit` and the other series that co-move with the two named ones have
their means shifted along with them, and the optimizer sees no spread to
trade. `r moved(W[, "centroid_as_views"])` weights move by more than half a
point against `r moved(W[, "centroid_direct"])` for the direct tilt, and
turnover falls from
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sum(abs(W[, "centroid_direct"] - w_mkt)) / 2)` to
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sum(abs(W[, "centroid_as_views"] - w_mkt)) / 2)`.
The weights that stop moving are the hedges: the government and credit
series the direct tilt had bought and sold to isolate `US_credit` against
its neighbors. What remains is a position in the two assets the opinion
named, with every other weight the market weight rescaled by the one factor
`r sprintf("%.3f", ratio[[1]])` that keeps the portfolio fully invested, which
is @eq-17-weights with two absolute views.

#### Exercise 4

```{r}
#| label: sol-17-ex4
Req <- Re[, eq_classes]
ord_rev <- match(rev(names(sort(mu_s[eq_classes]))), colnames(Req))   # reverse of the sample order
mr  <- suppressMessages(meucci.ranking(Req, p0, ord_rev))
mu_rank <- setNames(as.numeric(mr$mu), eq_classes)
set.seed(1602)
c_rev <- setNames(ac.ranking(Req, ord_rev), eq_classes)
rbind(sample = mu_s[eq_classes] * 12, entropy = mu_rank * 12, centroid = c_rev)[, colnames(Req)[ord_rev]] |> round(4)
c(ties = sum(abs(diff(mu_rank[colnames(Req)[ord_rev]])) < 1e-6),
  entropy_tangency_top = names(which.max(tangency_lo(mu_rank, mr$sigma))),
  centroid_tangency_top = names(which.max(tangency_lo(c_rev, S[eq_classes, eq_classes]))))
```

Reversing the sample order is the hardest ranking the data can be asked to
honor, and the entropy solution honors it in the only way a weak inequality
allows: all `r sum(abs(diff(mu_rank[colnames(Req)[ord_rev]])) < 1e-6) + 1L`
means are tied at `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mu_rank[[1]] * 12)`, which is
the isotonic regression of a decreasing sequence onto an increasing one. The
optimizer then sorts by covariance alone and holds
`r names(which.max(tangency_lo(mu_rank, mr$sigma)))` most. `ac.ranking()`
returns the centroid with `r names(which.max(c_rev))` at
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * max(c_rev) * 12)` a year and
`r names(which.min(c_rev))` at the same number below zero, a spacing the
reversal never asserted and a scale nothing in the data supports. A reader
who believed the reversal has an ordering and nothing else, so the honest
input is the centroid direction added to the equilibrium prior at a scale
they choose and state, as @tbl-17-ranking does with the prior's own
dispersion; handed alone to a tangency solver it buys
`r names(which.max(tangency_lo(c_rev, S[eq_classes, eq_classes])))` and
nothing else.
